result:
Done — US Suspense is clean for March.

**What I found:** Six bank-feed charges had posted as Dr 2900 Suspense / Cr 1000 Cash with no support, totaling $3,134.85.

**What I did:** Located the matching receipt for each one (all tie to the cent), posted six reclass entries (Dr expense / Cr Suspense) with the receipt attached to each:

| Merchant | Amount | Account |
|---|---|---|
| Delta Air Lines | 642.18 | 6300 Travel |
| Marriott Chicago | 418.90 | 6300 Travel |
| Blue Plate Bistro | 186.45 | 6310 Meals & Entertainment |
| Figma | 540.00 | 6200 Software Subscriptions |
| Staples | 97.32 | 6600 Office Supplies |
| LinkedIn Ads | 1,250.00 | 6410 Advertising |

**2900 Suspense now nets to $0.00** for March activity and ending balance.

A few judgment calls worth your eye:
- **Figma $540** — single-month Organization plan, under the $1,000 prepaid threshold, so expensed rather than deferred to 1210.
- **LinkedIn $1,250** — coded to 6410 Advertising (paid media) rather than 6400 Marketing Programs.
- **Blue Plate** — split to 6310 rather than lumping into travel, since the M&E deductibility treatment differs.

I also attached the receipts to the six *original* bank-feed entries, which had posted without support — that's a policy requirement, and it leaves the audit trail complete on both sides of the reclass.

Two things I deliberately did **not** do: these entries don't touch cash, so the March bank rec is unaffected, and I left all US checklist items at their current status since bank rec, depreciation, prepaids, payroll accrual, AP cutoff, intercompany and flux were outside this task and remain open. No exceptions were needed — every item was fully supported.
